# YuvexPay

> YuvexPay is a Brazilian payment gateway. The public REST API at `https://api.yuvexpay.com/v1/*` lets developers accept payments (PIX, credit and debit cards, boleto), issue refunds, move money out via PIX withdrawals, and manage products, coupons, customers, statements and webhooks.

All requests authenticate with a YuvexPay API key sent as a Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer ypk_<env>_<kid>_<secret>`. `<env>` is `test` (sandbox) or `live` (production). The same base URL serves both environments.

Write endpoints (`POST /v1/payments`, `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund`, `POST /v1/withdrawals`, `POST /v1/products`, `POST /v1/customers`) require an `X-Idempotency-Key` header. `POST /v1/coupons` honours the header when sent but does not require it.

All amounts are in **BRL** as decimal numbers (e.g. `49.90`), not cents.

## Documentation

- [Quickstart](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/quickstart): Create your first payment with a PIX QR code in under 5 minutes.
- [Authentication](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/authentication): API key format (`ypk_<env>_<kid>_<secret>`), scopes (`coupons:read` and `coupons:write` for the coupon API), IP allowlist, rotation, and `GET /v1/auth/self` for self-introspection.
- [Idempotency](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/idempotency): The `X-Idempotency-Key` contract: 24h TTL, 100-char limit, scoped per company and environment, payload-mismatch detection. Only `2xx` responses are stored and replayed, plus a `502 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` on a boleto payment: a same-key retry replays that `502` and never submits a second charge. A same-key retry of an earlier card payment request now returns `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` instead of the stored response (`201` or `502`): recover that payment with `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}`, or with a create with the same `externalId`, `mode: "hosted"` and `methods: ["CARD"]`, no `card` object or card fields, and a new key.
- [Errors](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/errors): Standard error envelope and the full code list (auth, validation, idempotency, payment, refund and withdrawal codes). `PROVIDER_REJECTED` (`400`) means the payment was refused, with a generic message that does not say why; `PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` (`502` or `503`) means retry later; on a boleto payment a `502` means the outcome is not known yet (see the Payments guide), and on a PIX payment a `502` or `503` means the payment was recorded `CANCELLED`, so retry with a new `externalId`. `CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` (`400`) means the request carried card data or asked for `CARD` in headless mode: cards go through the hosted checkout only. `CARD_HOLDER_INFO_REQUIRED`, `CARD_REMOTE_IP_REQUIRED` and `INSTALLMENTS_NOT_SUPPORTED` can no longer be returned. `PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED` (`403`, `details.method`) means a method in `methods` is not enabled for the account; if card payments are enabled for the account but card acceptance is temporarily unavailable, it is returned only when `CARD` is the only method. Split platform codes: `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` (`400`, `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`) means a split to an approved platform is above its fee cap; `SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED` (`400`, `details.recipientCompanyId`) means the platform's approval was withdrawn; `SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID` (`403`, no `details`) means the key in `X-Split-Platform-Key` was refused, one answer for every reason; `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`400`, `details.limit`) means a platform connection would take the seller past its limit of active partners. Cart codes on `POST /v1/payments`, all `400` top-level codes: `AMOUNT_ITEMS_MISMATCH` (`amount` is not the sum of `items`, with `details.amount` and `details.itemsTotal` as a string), `AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH`, `MINIMUM_AMOUNT_FOR_CARD_OR_BOLETO`, `ITEM_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`, `OFFER_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`, `UPSELL_AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH` and `COUPON_INVALID` (one answer for every unusable coupon); `orderBump` or `upsell` on a headless payment returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with `OFFERS_REQUIRE_HOSTED` in the message. Coupon API codes: `COUPON_VALUE_INVALID`, `COUPON_WINDOW_INVALID`, `COUPON_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` (`400`) and `COUPON_CODE_TAKEN` (`409`). A refund of a `FREE` payment returns `400 INVALID_STATUS`.
- [Rate limiting](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/rate-limiting): Per-company limits, response headers (`X-RateLimit-*`), and exponential backoff guidance.
- [Environments](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/environments): Sandbox vs. production. Same URL, different key prefix.
- [Sandbox testing](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/sandbox): Deterministic recipes. **A sandbox payment is never terminal in the `POST /v1/payments` response — a status check about 5 seconds later writes the outcome — except a headless free order, already `FREE` there.** Payment cents, the same for `PIX`, `CARD` and `BOLETO`: `.01` paid, `.02` stays unpaid forever, `.03` cancelled, `.04` expired, `.05` paid (MED is not reachable from the amount), any other cents paid. The cents are read from the payment `amount` you send, before any fee passed to the payer (`passFeeToPayer`), and from the final `amount` after a coupon, line item changes or an order bump. Coupons are per environment, and a sandbox free order is never charged the free order fee. Nothing is charged: a sandbox card goes through the hosted checkout, which accepts any test card number that passes the Luhn check (for example `4111 1111 1111 1111`), never stores the full card number or the security code, and never asks for a 3D Secure challenge; a card charged in sandbox is always recorded as `credit` in `methodData.cardFundingType`, whatever test card number you use, so `debit` cannot be produced in sandbox; a sandbox boleto carries a valid-format test digitable line and barcode, and `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/boleto` returns a generated test PDF that says it must not be paid. Sandbox refunds work for `PIX`, `CARD` and `BOLETO`: payment cents `.02` make the refund fail with `PSP_REFUND_FAILED`, any other cents succeed, read from the payment amount and not from the refund amount. Withdrawal cents `.01` completed, `.02`/`.03` failed, `.04` stays processing, reached synchronously. `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate` forces a terminal status with no wait: `PAID` (default), `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`, `REFUNDED`, `DISPUTED`; sandbox keys only: a production key gets `403 FORBIDDEN`, and a production payment id gets `404` because a sandbox key cannot see it. Splits in sandbox: the invite, accept and split cycle works without the KYC gate. **The split platform connection works in sandbox too, with a `ypk_test_` key of the approved company in `X-Split-Platform-Key`, the same fee cap and no notification to the seller; the approved production company is then the one recipient a sandbox payment can name outside sandbox mode.** **Sandbox sends no webhooks to a configured endpoint, for any event type — poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` and use `/simulate` instead.**
- [Payments guide](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/payments): Headless PIX, headless BOLETO, and the hosted checkout (PIX, CARD, BOLETO). Lifecycle from `NEW` to `PAID`/`REFUNDED`, plus `FREE`. **Line items: optional `items` on `POST /v1/payments`, 1 to 50 lines of `name` (1-120), `unitAmount` (BRL, > 0, at most 2 decimals), `quantity` (1-999), optional `productId` (a product of the account in the key's environment, else `400 ITEM_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`) and `sku` (1-64); the amount is their sum, `amount` can be omitted and, when sent, must match exactly (`400 AMOUNT_ITEMS_MISMATCH`, `details.itemsTotal`); `itemsQuantityEditable: true` lets the payer change quantities on the hosted checkout before picking a method (not with a `FIXED` split). Payments carry `items` (`id`, `name`, `unitAmount`, `quantity`, `kind` `ITEM`/`ORDER_BUMP`/`UPSELL`, `productId`, `sku`), `subtotal`, `discount` and `coupon` (`{ code }` or `null`), and `amount` = `subtotal` - `discount`; list, detail and txid responses also carry `parentPaymentId` and `completedAt`. On a hosted payment `amount` can change before method selection (quantities, order bump, coupon), so read the final amount from the API or the webhook.** **Coupons: created in the dashboard (Vendas > Cupons) or with `/v1/coupons`; applied with `couponCode` on `POST /v1/payments` or in the Cupom field of the hosted checkout before a method is picked; the field shows only when at least one active coupon can apply to that payment (inside its validity window, with uses left, covering the whole order or one of its products, of the payment's environment), and the page learns only whether a coupon can apply, never which codes exist. `PERCENT` (`percentBp`, 1-10000 basis points, rounded half up in centavos) or `FIXED` (`amount`, never more than the covered lines); `productIds` limits the discount to those lines (the order bump included when listed), empty covers the whole order. Every unusable code gets `400 COUPON_INVALID`; codes are case-insensitive; `validFrom` inclusive, `validUntil` exclusive; a use is held while the payment is open, given back on expiry or cancellation and kept on payment or `FREE`; `maxRedemptionsPerBuyer` is checked against the payer e-mail when known (`customer.email` at create, the checkout e-mail when the method is picked, where an over-limit coupon is removed); coupons are per environment; a `FIXED` split takes no coupon; a discount below R$ 5.00 leaves PIX only on the hosted checkout.** **Free orders: a coupon covering the whole amount ends the payment `FREE` with no charge, at once on a headless create (`201`, `status: "FREE"`, `amount: 0`, `methodData: null`) or when the payer confirms on the hosted checkout. `amount`, `feeAmount`, `netAmount` are `0`, `paidAt` is `null`, `completedAt` is set; not refundable (`400 INVALID_STATUS`), no merchant receipt (`400 RECEIPT_NOT_AVAILABLE`); the merchant is charged the fixed part of its PIX fee (no percentage, no minimum, nothing in sandbox), debited even into a negative balance and shown in the statement as `Taxa de pedido gratuito`; webhook `PAYMENT_FREE`, never `PAYMENT_PAID`; plugins get `payment.free`, so the conversion plugins, which listen for `payment.paid`, do not report it as a purchase; the payer still gets the receipt e-mail and the purchase page; `GET /v1/payments?status=FREE` lists them.** **Hosted only: `orderBump` (`name`, `unitAmount` > 0, optional `description` up to 500 and `productId`, else `400 OFFER_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`) is a box the payer ticks before picking a method, added to `items` as `ORDER_BUMP`; `upsell` (same fields, `unitAmount` from R$ 1.00 up to the payment `amount` after the coupon, else `400 UPSELL_AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH`) is offered for 30 minutes on the success screen of a `PAID` or `CONFIRMED` payment and, when accepted, becomes a new payment with `parentPaymentId`, one `UPSELL` item, the same payer and splits, 30-minute expiry, no payer fee and no recovery kit, paid by PIX or in one click with the same card from the browser that paid by card; it carries none of the merchant's `metadata` except `cancelUrl` and no `externalId`, so link it through `parentPaymentId`. Both return `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with `OFFERS_REQUIRE_HOSTED` in headless mode and are not offered with a `FIXED` split; the upsell is never offered on a `FREE` payment, nor when checkout changes took the final `amount` below its price.** **With `passFeeToPayer`, the create response fee is for the first method, the checkout shows each method's own total, and the fee is computed again at the rate of the method the payer picks, card included (single installment).** **Card payments are accepted only through the hosted checkout: `POST /v1/payments` rejects a `card` object, `CARD` in `methods` in headless mode (`mode` omitted or `headless`), and any of `deviceInfo`, `remoteIp`, `holderInfo`, `authorizeOnly`, `creditCard`, `creditCardHolderInfo`, `creditCardToken`, `installmentCount`, `installmentValue`, `totalValue` at the top level of the body, with `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API`, even without a valid API key; the card data is not stored or logged. To charge a card, create the payment with `mode: "hosted"` and `CARD` in `methods` (`["CARD"]`, or `["PIX", "CARD"]` to let the payer choose), with an `amount` of at least `R$ 5.00`, and redirect the payer to the returned `checkoutUrl`. The checkout collects the card (credit in a single installment, or debit) and runs 3D Secure itself. The result arrives as `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED`, `PAYMENT_PAID`, `PAYMENT_EXPIRED` or `PAYMENT_CANCELLED`, or poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`.** A hosted card payment whose 3D Secure challenge fails, or gets no answer for about 7 minutes, ends `EXPIRED` (`PAYMENT_EXPIRED`); a card refused after the challenge ends `CANCELLED` (`PAYMENT_CANCELLED` with `reason: payment_failed`); in both cases the payer cannot pick another method for it, so create a new payment. Payment links created in the dashboard use the same hosted checkout. **When a hosted payment with a `completionUrl` (or a dashboard payment link with a success URL; only an `http` or `https` URL of up to 2048 characters is used) reaches `PAID`, `CONFIRMED` or `FREE`, the checkout counts down 5 seconds and redirects there (while a post-purchase upsell is on screen it shows only the Ir agora button), adding `yvx_payment_id`, `yvx_status` (`PAID`, `CONFIRMED` or `FREE`), `yvx_amount_cents` (the final payment `amount` in integer centavos, after the coupon and checkout changes, `0` on `FREE`, without the fee added for the payer), `yvx_reference` (`metadata.externalReference`, which a payment link fills with its reference, else `externalId`, else empty but still present), `yvx_ts` (unix seconds) and `yvx_signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `${payment_id}.${status}.${amount_cents}.${reference}.${ts}` over the URL-decoded values, keyed with the account's 64-character redirect secret used as-is as UTF-8 bytes (not hex-decoded).** The merchant's own query parameters are kept and any `yvx_` parameter is replaced. The secret is in the dashboard under Configurações > Checkout, Segredo do redirecionamento; it signs sandbox and production redirects, is created on first use, and rotating it (Trocar segredo) makes URLs signed earlier fail at once. Verify with a constant-time compare, reject when `yvx_ts` is more than 600 seconds from your clock, and confirm the payment with `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` or the webhook before fulfilling: the redirect is not proof of payment and can repeat for the same payment with a new `yvx_ts`. Test vector: secret `0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f00f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0`; `3f2b8c1e-5d4a-4b6f-9e7d-1a2b3c4d5e6f.PAID.4990.order-1234.1793462400` signs to `ac8008714e1cb1e8475801af038e00c0fb7e8ed710be046d0bc4467c18667ab2`, and `3f2b8c1e-5d4a-4b6f-9e7d-1a2b3c4d5e6f.CONFIRMED.10000..1793462400` (empty reference) to `e4ab206280ece8a96ff03c854ed96e0207b01cb1c0ec0924e998ed0e30c96976`. `skip_customer=1` (or `true`) on the `checkoutUrl` skips the payer form only when the payment already has a customer with a name of 2 to 120 characters, a valid e-mail and a CPF or CNPJ with valid check digits; on a payment with such a customer, the wait for `CHECKOUT_ABANDONED` and the recovery kit start the first time the checkout is opened while the payment is in `PENDING_METHOD_SELECTION`, with or without the flag. `skip_address=1` has no effect today because the API has no address fields. Personal data in the checkout URL is ignored, and payment link URLs do not read the flags. **Optional `recoveryKit: boolean` on `POST /v1/payments` turns the recovery kit on or off for the payment (omitted: the account default, off until turned on in the dashboard under Configurações > Checkout, Kit de recuperação; a dashboard payment link has its own setting in the link form, and the payment detail shows the kit with a Ligar kit or Parar e-mails button). The kit e-mails a payer whose details the hosted checkout saved, or whose complete customer the checkout was opened with, and who did not pay: up to 5 e-mails at the account's delays (default 15 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours after the kit started, each 5 minutes to 7 days), plus one about 10 minutes before a PIX code expires, sent only while the payment can still be paid (set `expiresInMinutes` to cover the delays; a payment-link payment keeps e-mailing a link to the active payment link), stopped when it is paid. A fixed price per kit, shown in the dashboard and not in `GET /public/pricing`, is debited once, when the first e-mail is sent, whether or not the payer pays, even if the balance goes negative; a kit that sends nothing is not charged, and the statement shows the debit as `Kit de recuperação`. Headless payments never start a kit, sandbox payments never get one, and a second payment of the same payment link by a payer whose kit is still running gets none. `GET /v1/payments`, `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` and `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}` return `recoveryKit: { enabled, charged, emailsSent }`. Recovery reports are on the Recuperação de vendas card of Visão geral, and order bump and upsell reports on its Order bump e upsell card; the offers filled in for new payment links are set under Configurações > Checkout.** **The payer sees the store name, the company's display name (Nome da loja, 2 to 60 characters, asked when the company is created and edited with the logo and color under Configurações > Checkout), in the checkout header and legal line, the purchase page, receipts and e-mails sent as `<store name> via YuvexPay`; a company registered with a CPF never shows the holder's name or CPF, a company with a CNPJ also shows its razão social and CNPJ in the legal line, and a company without a valid store name shows YuvexPay until one is set. The receipt e-mail to the payer is on by default and turned off under Configurações > Checkout (E-mail de recibo ao comprador). Payer e-mails stop for an address, for every store, after a hard bounce, an invalid-address block or a spam report, and stop for your store after the address unsubscribes. A payer can sign in with their e-mail to download their data as JSON or delete their account; deletion needs a fresh identity check, is refused while a linked payment has a pending charge, a refund in progress, an open dispute, MED or chargeback, or an open refund request, keeps the payment records required for financial and anti-money-laundering retention, erases or anonymizes the rest and stops running recovery kits.** `metadata.cancelUrl` (an `http` or `https` URL of up to 2048 characters; any other value is ignored, not rejected) shows a back link to that URL on the hosted checkout while the payment is unpaid, and a payment link's cancel URL does the same on the payments the link creates. Card payments must be enabled for the account; until they are, a create with `CARD` in `methods` returns `403 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED`. Card acceptance also requires the account owner's e-mail to be confirmed, and YuvexPay's risk controls can suspend it temporarily; on an account with card payments enabled, while card acceptance is unavailable, other methods keep working, the hosted checkout does not offer `CARD` (payments and payment links created earlier included), a create with `CARD` and other methods succeeds without `CARD`, and a create whose only method is `CARD` returns `403 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED`. Card payments already created with card data through the API keep working: `GET` returns their masked card `methodData`, and webhooks, refunds and chargebacks are unchanged. On a card payment `methodData.cardFundingType` is `credit`, `debit`, or `null` when the funding type is not known (older payments included); webhook bodies do not carry it. Boleto errors on create: `400 PROVIDER_REJECTED` = refused, generic message, payment recorded `CANCELLED`; `503 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` = charge not created, payment recorded `CANCELLED`, retry later with a new `externalId`; `502 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` = outcome not known yet, the payment stays `PROCESSING` (with `methodData: null`) until resolved (15 minutes or more) and then continues or ends `CANCELLED`. **The `502` is stored for the `X-Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key replays that `502` for 24h and never submits a second charge. Send `externalId` on every boleto payment. To recover after a `502`, repeat the request ONCE with the same `externalId` and a new `X-Idempotency-Key`: it returns the existing payment (its `id`) without a new charge; then poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` until it leaves `PROCESSING`, and create a new payment with a new `externalId` if it ends `CANCELLED`.** Do not poll by repeating the create: a same-key repeat replays the same response for 24h. `methodData` is `null` while a boleto payment is `PROCESSING` after a `502`, and on a payment recorded `CANCELLED` before a charge was created. Without `externalId`, a request with a new key creates a new payment, so the payer can end up with two boletos for the same order. A PIX payment whose create returns `502` or `503` is recorded `CANCELLED`: retry with a new `externalId`. **A payment can be split with other YuvexPay companies through the optional `splits` array on creation: `recipientCompanyId`, `type` (`PERCENTAGE` or `FIXED`) and `value`, set at creation only — there is no endpoint to add, edit or remove a split afterwards.** Shares are computed from `amount` (the gross) and the YuvexPay fee is always the originating company's, never apportioned. `netAmount` stays pre-split: the originator keeps `netAmount` minus the sum of the splits. The sum must be `<= netAmount`, otherwise `SPLIT_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_NET` and nothing is clamped. **Percentage shares round DOWN to the cent and every remaining cent stays with the originating company.** Splitting is opt-in per company pair, per environment and per direction: **the ORIGINATING company invites the recipient by company ID in its dashboard (Configurações > Parceiros de divisão) and the recipient accepts** (`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` until it does, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` once it refuses, and a refused pair needs a new dashboard invitation). States are `PENDING`, `ACCEPTED` (the active state), `DECLINED`, `REVOKED` and `CANCELLED` (invite withdrawn by the originator). Either side can revoke an active pair (`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`), and **revocation is forward-only, so payments already created still settle, refund and freeze normally.** Re-inviting after `DECLINED`/`REVOKED`/`CANCELLED` creates a NEW relationship and keeps the old one as history. Invite/accept/decline/revoke are dashboard-only — there is no API for them — but `GET /v1/splits/partners` lists the pairs so an integration can discover usable IDs. **The one exception is a split platform approved by YuvexPay: it connects a seller on the seller's first payment, with no invitation, by sending its own API key in `X-Split-Platform-Key` on `POST /v1/payments`, in production and in sandbox, and every split to it is limited by a fee cap (`SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED`); see the Split platforms guide.** Active partners are capped per company (three by default); that ceiling is enforced in the dashboard at invite/accept time, and the public API returns it only when a platform connection would exceed it (`SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `details.limit`). Both companies must be approved (KYC, plus KYB for a business) at invite time and again when the payment is created; **in sandbox the KYC gate does not apply, so the whole cycle is testable, the platform connection included.** **Recipients get no webhook and no receipt**: the payment is not theirs, `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` returns `404` for them, and they see the money only in `GET /v1/balance`, in `GET /v1/documents/statements` and in their dashboard. A split credit follows the **recipient's own** rolling reserve policy, not the originator's. Splits are environment-locked (`SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH`). **The optional `tracking` object on `POST /v1/payments` carries attribution data to the conversion plugins enabled for the account (GA4, Meta Conversions API, TikTok Events API, UTMify): `utmSource`, `utmMedium`, `utmCampaign`, `utmTerm`, `utmContent`, `src`, `sck`, `fbclid`, `gclid` (strings up to 512 characters), `ttclid` (up to 1000), `gaClientId` (GA4 client id `<digits>.<digits>`, or a raw `_ga` cookie value `GA1.1.<a>.<b>`, stored as `<a>.<b>`), `fbp` and `fbc` (the Meta `_fbp` and `_fbc` cookie values).** Values are trimmed; a `gaClientId`, `fbp` or `fbc` that does not match its format is ignored, while a non-string or over-long value in any other field returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Without `fbc`, an `fbc` is built from `fbclid` for Meta. The hosted checkout fills the fields left empty from its URL (`utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_term`, `utm_content`, `src`, `sck`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `ttclid`, `_ga`, `_fbp`, `_fbc` query parameters) and from the `_ga`, `_fbp` and `_fbc` cookies of the checkout's own domain; values sent at creation are kept. **The merchant's own `_ga`, `_fbp` and `_fbc` cookies live on the merchant's domain and the checkout cannot read them: send them in `tracking` when creating the payment, or append them, URL-encoded, as query parameters to `checkoutUrl`.**
- [Split platforms](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/split-platforms): For marketplaces and checkouts that create payments with the seller's API key and take a share through `splits`. Approval is granted by YuvexPay, company by company, with a fee cap agreed at approval (contact support). **An approved platform connects a seller on the first payment: `POST /v1/payments` with the seller's key in `Authorization`, the platform's company in `splits[]` and the platform's own key, without `Bearer`, in `X-Split-Platform-Key`. The relationship is recorded as `ACCEPTED` with the cap, the seller is notified in production, and the payment is created on the same call.** A connection opens no split request and does not count toward the seller's limit of pending requests. A request from the seller that is already pending, a dashboard invitation or one that an earlier payment opened without the header, is accepted by that call. The header is read only when exactly one recipient in `splits[]` has no accepted relationship with the seller; otherwise it is ignored, so a connected seller never depends on the platform key. The platform key must be an active key in the environment of the seller's key with `payments:write`, used from inside its IP allowlist, from a company other than the seller's: otherwise `403 SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID`, one answer for every reason. **A call that does not connect follows the regular flow, in production and in sandbox: it returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` and opens a pending request to each recipient that has no relationship with the seller yet and can receive splits in that environment (an active company, in the same environment as the request and, in production, with verification approved); for any other company ID the answer is the same and no request is opened. The platform accepts the request in its dashboard, or a later call with the header accepts it. That is the case without the header, with a valid key whose company is not the recipient or is not an approved platform, and with two or more recipients that have no accepted relationship; past the seller's limit of pending requests the call returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`.** `SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID`, `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` and `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` open no request. Send the header from a server only; it is not allowed on cross-origin browser requests. **Fee cap: a percentage of `amount` (the gross). The cap applied is the lowest of the cap recorded on the relationship, the platform's current cap and the maximum YuvexPay allows; a lowered cap applies at once, a raised one does not reach sellers already connected. `PERCENTAGE` must be at most the cap; `FIXED` must be at most `amount × cap / 100`, not rounded up. Above it: `400 SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` with `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`, checked before anything is recorded, so a first payment above the cap connects nobody.** A request the platform accepts by hand in its dashboard is capped too: the relationship records the platform's cap at the time it accepts, returned as `feeCap`, and each split is limited by the same three values. `GET /v1/splits/partners?direction=INCOMING&status=ACCEPTED` lists the sellers connected to the platform; without `status` the list also carries pending, declined, revoked and cancelled pairs. A seller with no active partner slot left gets `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. In production the seller gets a dashboard notification and an e-mail naming the platform and the cap, and can revoke under Configurações > Parceiros de divisão; either side can revoke. A request the platform accepts by hand sends the seller the notice of any accepted invitation, which does not name the cap. **A pair that was revoked, or that the platform once declined, is never reconnected by the header (`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED`), even after a later invitation was cancelled: the seller sends a new dashboard invitation and the platform accepts it in its dashboard.** While that invitation is pending, payments return `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`; if the seller cancels it, a payment with the header returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED` or `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` again, and one without the header opens a new pending request and returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`. If YuvexPay withdraws the approval, every new payment with a split to the platform fails with `400 SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED` for sellers connected with a fee cap, the header connects no new seller (the call follows the regular flow), and payments already created are not changed. If the approval is given back, connected sellers work again under the same lowest-of-three cap rule, with the platform's new cap. A payment link does not connect a platform: it is refused with `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` and follows the regular flow; once the seller is connected, links follow the same cap. The connection works in sandbox under the same rules: the seller's `ypk_test_` key in `Authorization` and a `ypk_test_` key of the approved company in `X-Split-Platform-Key`; approval is granted in production only and the sandbox connection applies the same fee cap, with no notification to the seller. Environments are kept apart: a connection, revocation or decline in one does not reach the other. The approved company is a production company, so it is the one recipient a sandbox payment can name outside sandbox mode, once connected in sandbox; before that, a `ypk_test_` payment that names it without the header returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`, opens no request and leaves nothing to accept. The seller should give the platform a key limited to the payments scopes with an IP allowlist, never a `*` key.
- [Refunds](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/refunds): Eligibility rules, lifecycle, and error codes (`REFUND_IN_PROGRESS`, `REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `REFUND_REQUIRES_MANUAL_REVIEW`, etc.). Eligibility is enforced by `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund` itself; the payment detail response carries no eligibility field. **A payment can be refunded once, fully or partially: a `PARTIAL_REFUND` payment is not refundable again (`400 REFUND_ALREADY_PERFORMED`), a `REFUNDED` one returns `400 ALREADY_REFUNDED`, and a refund requested while another is being processed returns `400 REFUND_IN_PROGRESS`.** **Partial refunds are conditional, not unsupported: they require a payment that has already settled and a processing route that supports them, otherwise `PARTIAL_REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED`. A full refund is always available on a refundable payment.** On a payment with splits the refund is proportional: every party is debited in proportion to what it received, the originating company included, and partial refunds use the same proportions. A recipient that already withdrew its share goes negative and the shortfall is never moved onto the originating company, so `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE_FOR_REFUND` is measured against the originating company's share only. A PIX MED freezes each party's proportional share the same way. **In production a payer can request a refund of a paid payment on YuvexPay's purchase page, up to 90 days after the payment; the merchant answers in the dashboard (Vendas > Disputas > Reembolsos), with an optional automatic approval of requests made within 7 days of the payment, and there is no API for requests. An approved request is a full refund with the same rules, fees and `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE_FOR_REFUND` check as `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund`, with `reason: "Pedido de reembolso do comprador"`. As a last resort, after a refused, unanswered or failed request, YuvexPay can refund the payment itself with `reason: "Reembolso feito pela YuvexPay"`: like a PIX MED or a chargeback, the merchant is debited the full amount returned to the payer, YuvexPay keeps the processing fee, and the balance check does not apply, so the available balance can go negative.** Both send the usual `PAYMENT_REFUNDED` / `PAYMENT_REFUND_FAILED` bodies, which carry no reason; read it with `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refunds`. Because they do not go through the integration, the merchant's own refund call can get `REFUND_IN_PROGRESS` or `ALREADY_REFUNDED`.
- [Withdrawals](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/withdrawals): PIX-only, BRL-only, daily/nightly limits, masked `pixKey`, and the never-retry rule on ambiguous `PROCESSING` (whose horizon is hours, not minutes). **`amount` is the NET the recipient receives; the flat fee is added on top, so the balance is debited `grossAmount = amount + feeAmount`.** Gross is what `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, the daily/nightly `used` counter and the per-transaction cap are measured against; the minimum is measured against the net and is `R$ 10.00` unless raised for the account — read `minAmount` from `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`. The creditor document sent to the network resolves in three steps: `destination.recipientDocument` when sent, else the PIX key itself when it is a CPF or CNPJ key, else your own tax id. `creditorDocumentSource` is dashboard-only and returns `400 CREDITOR_DOCUMENT_SOURCE_NOT_SUPPORTED` on the public API. Per-transaction caps are account-dependent and come from `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`, not a fixed platform maximum. `errorMessage` is returned by `GET /v1/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}` only, never by the list. `providerErrorCode` is on both and carries only a rejection code reported by the receiving institution (`AC03`, `AC06`, `AC07`, `AG03`, `AM18`, `RR04`, `SL02`, `BE01`, `CH11`, `PIX_KEY_NOT_FOUND`, `PIX_KEY_OWNER_MISMATCH`, `ACCOUNT_CLOSED`, `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`), otherwise `null`.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/guides/webhooks): `v1` HMAC-SHA256 signature with timestamp anti-replay (`X-Webhook-Signature`, `X-Webhook-Timestamp`), at-least-once delivery, no order guarantees, retries. **`X-Webhook-Delivery-Id` is the same on every automatic retry of a delivery; `X-Webhook-Attempt` increments, and each attempt sends the same body bytes as the first, signed again with a new `X-Webhook-Timestamp` and `X-Webhook-Signature`, so verify each attempt against its own raw body. A resend from the dashboard or by support takes the event type of the payment's or withdrawal's current status and sends the exact bytes of the latest original delivery of that event for that resource (not its current state) as a new delivery to every endpoint active and subscribed to the event now, with a new delivery id, attempt `1` and a new timestamp and signature over those bytes; it is refused with `400` `NO_EVENT_FOR_STATUS` (the status sends no webhook), `NO_WEBHOOK_CONFIGURED` (no active endpoint subscribed to the event), `NO_DELIVERY_TO_RESEND` (the event never went out for that resource: sandbox, or no endpoint active and subscribed when it happened), `WEBHOOK_RESEND_UNAVAILABLE` (an older delivery whose exact body can no longer be reproduced; deliveries made from 2026-11-01 on can always be resent) or `WEBHOOK_RESEND_RATE_LIMITED` (wait about 30 seconds between resends of the same event); each test ping is a new delivery too. There is no event id: deduplicate on event type + resource id + status (`refundId` for refund events, `medId` + `resolution` for MED events), checked against your current state of the resource, not on the delivery id alone.** **The HTTP body is the bare event object — there is no `{ id, type, data }` envelope and the event name is carried only in the `X-Webhook-Event` header.** Fourteen subscribable event types. **`PAYMENT_FREE` is opt-in per endpoint (dashboard label Pagamento gratuito (cupom 100%)): sent when a coupon covered the whole amount and the order completed without a charge, never for sandbox; a free order never sends `PAYMENT_PAID`. Body `{ id, txId, status: "FREE", amount: 0, paidAt, endToEndId: null, payer }`, where `paidAt` is the completion time (the API returns it as `completedAt`, with `paidAt: null`) and `payer` has no institution. A resend of a `FREE` payment is a `PAYMENT_FREE` with the original body. A post-purchase upsell payment sends webhooks for an `id` the integration never created: read it and follow `parentPaymentId`.** **`CHECKOUT_ABANDONED` is opt-in per endpoint: it is delivered only to endpoints that selected it (dashboard label **Checkout abandonado**), and existing endpoints do not get it until edited. It is sent at most once per payment when the hosted checkout saved the payer's name, e-mail and CPF or CNPJ (payment links included; saved as soon as all three are filled in and valid, or on open when the browser remembered them), or, for a payment created with a customer that has a name of 2 to 120 characters, a valid e-mail and a valid CPF or CNPJ, from the first time the checkout is opened while the payment is in `PENDING_METHOD_SELECTION` (with or without `skip_customer=1`), and the payment is still unpaid 30 minutes later (a platform-wide delay set by YuvexPay that can change); never for headless payments, sandbox payments or a manual resend, and not when it would go out more than 24 hours late. Body `{ id, txId, status, amount, buyer }`, all five always present, `status` being the current unpaid status (`PENDING_METHOD_SELECTION`, `NEW`, `PROCESSING`, `EXPIRED` or `CANCELLED`) and `buyer` being `{ name, email, phone }`, never `null` itself: `name` is the name sent in `customer` completed with the one typed on the checkout, `email` and `phone` are the ones typed on the checkout else the ones sent in `customer`, each falling back to the linked customer record and `null` when not known. It can arrive after `PAYMENT_EXPIRED` or `PAYMENT_CANCELLED`, and the payment can still be paid later, so read `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` before contacting the payer; that response carries the same contact in `payer.email` and `payer.phone`.** `PAYMENT_PAID` carries a `payer` block (name, CPF/CNPJ, institution name + ISPB) plus the network `endToEndId`; `payer.document` carries a masked string (for example `***405566**`) when no full document is on file, and is `null` only when neither was captured. `WITHDRAWAL_SENT` carries a `recipient` block, populated when the withdrawal had a recipient document. Both blocks are `null` when every field would be null. **Webhooks are delivered for production activity only: sandbox payments and withdrawals send no webhooks to a configured endpoint, for any event type, because an endpoint belongs to the account and not to an environment.** A sandbox integration polls `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` and forces terminal outcomes with `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate`; the dashboard **Send test** button delivers a signed `TEST` event to exercise a verifier. `MED_RECEIVED.providerMedId` is always `null` when present, `source` on `PAYMENT_REFUNDED` and `MED_RESOLVED` is `merchant_refund` or `null`, and `PAYMENT_REFUND_FAILED.reason` is always `Reembolso não processado. O valor foi devolvido ao saldo.` `PAYMENT_CANCELLED.reason`, when present, is `payment_failed` (payment refused or not completed, such as a card refused after 3D Secure) or `payment_cancelled` (charge cancelled before payment); a failed or unanswered 3D Secure challenge sends `PAYMENT_EXPIRED` instead. `PAYMENT_REFUNDED` is also sent for refunds the merchant did not start: a payer's refund request approved in the dashboard or automatically, and a refund YuvexPay made after such a request. **When a card chargeback dispute is won, the chargeback debit is credited back (the processing fee stays with YuvexPay), the payment leaves `CHARGEBACK` for the status it had before (`PAID`, `CONFIRMED`, `REFUNDED` or `PARTIAL_REFUND`), and `PAYMENT_PAID` or `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED` is sent again for that status; a payment restored to `REFUNDED` or `PARTIAL_REFUND` sends no webhook.** An endpoint that keeps failing is suspended automatically and comes back only through `POST /app/companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/reactivate`, which sends a test delivery first (`400 REACTIVATION_PROBE_FAILED` when it does not answer `2xx`); `PATCH` with `isActive: true` on a suspended endpoint returns `400 WEBHOOK_SUSPENDED`. Each new suspension of the same endpoint waits longer before reactivation (currently none, then 15 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours and 24 hours, starting over after 7 days active), and each endpoint gets at most 5 reactivation test deliveries every 10 minutes; a reactivation that is too early returns `429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After`, `details.retryAfter`, `details.reactivationAvailableAt` and `details.reason` (`REACTIVATION_COOLDOWN` or `REACTIVATION_ATTEMPTS`), and `GET /app/companies/{companyId}/webhooks` returns `reactivationAvailableAt` per endpoint (`null` when not suspended).
- [Changelog](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/changelog): API changes, written in Portuguese. 2026-10-04, breaking: card payments are no longer accepted by `POST /v1/payments` (`400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API`), use the hosted checkout; sandbox `CARD` and `BOLETO` follow the payment cents table and sandbox refunds work for every method. 2026-10-04, debit cards: the hosted checkout also accepts debit cards, and card payments returned by `GET /v1/payments`, `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`, `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}`, `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate` and a create repeated with the same `externalId` carry the read-only `methodData.cardFundingType` (`credit`, `debit` or `null`); webhooks are unchanged. 2026-10-07, card availability: card acceptance requires the account owner's e-mail to be confirmed and can be suspended temporarily by risk controls; on an account with card payments enabled, while it is unavailable, the hosted checkout does not offer `CARD`, a create with other methods drops `CARD`, and a create with `CARD` as the only method returns `403 PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ENABLED`. 2026-10-11, webhook reactivation: each new suspension of the same webhook endpoint waits longer before it can be reactivated (none, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours, then 24 hours, starting over after 7 days active), a reactivation that is too early returns `429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `details.reactivationAvailableAt`, the webhook list returns `reactivationAvailableAt`, and `PATCH` with `isActive: true` on a suspended endpoint returns `400 WEBHOOK_SUSPENDED`. 2026-10-11, products and customers: `GET /v1/products` accepts `isActive` only as `true` or `false` (anything else returns `400`); each customer in `GET /v1/customers` carries `approvedCount`, `approvedAmount` and `lastApprovedAt` over its `PAID` and `CONFIRMED` payments, and its `isActive` filter now works (it returned `400` before). 2026-10-11, refunds: a refund that takes the counted volume of the merchant's verified CPF or CNPJ below an approved rewards prize keeps the processing fee, and the extra debit can take the available balance negative. 2026-10-31, cart: `POST /v1/payments` accepts `items`, `itemsQuantityEditable`, `couponCode`, `orderBump` and `upsell`; payments carry `items`, `subtotal`, `discount`, `coupon`, `parentPaymentId` and `completedAt`; new coupon API at `/v1/coupons` with the `coupons:read` and `coupons:write` scopes; new status `FREE` for orders a coupon covers in full, with the opt-in webhook `PAYMENT_FREE`; with `passFeeToPayer` the hosted checkout shows each method's total with that method's fee before the payer picks one.

## API reference

- [API overview](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/introduction)
- [Inspect API key](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/auth/self): `GET /v1/auth/self`
- [Create payment](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/create): `POST /v1/payments` — PIX supports `enforcePayerDocument` (best-effort same-document opt-in). `CARD` is hosted only: a `card` object, `CARD` in headless mode, or a card field at the top level of the body returns `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` with the message `Pagamentos com cartão não são aceitos pela API. Use o checkout hospedado: crie o pagamento com mode "hosted" e envie o pagador para o checkoutUrl.`, even without a valid API key. The `card` object and `methodData.challengeUrl` were removed, and `CARD_HOLDER_INFO_REQUIRED`, `CARD_REMOTE_IP_REQUIRED` and `INSTALLMENTS_NOT_SUPPORTED` can no longer be returned. A refused payment returns `400 PROVIDER_REJECTED`; `502` and `503` return `PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE`. A boleto `502` (outcome not known yet) is stored and replayed for the same `X-Idempotency-Key`: recover the payment by repeating the request once with the same `externalId` and a new key, then poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`. A PIX `502` or `503` is recorded `CANCELLED`. Optional `splits[]` (`recipientCompanyId`, `type`, `value`) shares the payment with other YuvexPay companies; the maximum number of entries is the recipient limit configured for the account, three by default. Split failures arrive as a top-level `error.code`, not inside `VALIDATION_ERROR.details`: `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `SPLIT_SELF_RECIPIENT`, `SPLIT_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_NET`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` (with `details.recipients`, the company IDs that declined), `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_INACTIVE`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_APPROVED`, `SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH`, `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED` (with `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`), `SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED` and `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (platform connection only, with `details.limit`) are `400`; `SPLIT_ORIGINATOR_NOT_APPROVED` and `SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID` are `403`. Optional header `X-Split-Platform-Key`: the API key of an approved split platform, sent without `Bearer`, which connects the seller to the platform named in `splits[]` on this call; it must be in the environment of the key in `Authorization`, works in production and in sandbox, and is read only when exactly one recipient has no accepted relationship, and ignored otherwise. **`SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` is the single answer for every recipient that cannot receive a split yet except a pair that declined an invitation from your company or was revoked — both need an invitation your company already sent, so a company ID you never invited reads the same whether or not it exists and the error cannot be used to enumerate company IDs.** `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_INACTIVE`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_APPROVED` and `SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH` are only returned for a recipient that had already accepted the relationship. There is no `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`. Outstanding consent requests are capped per company and environment (20 by default): beyond that, naming a new recipient returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`. The response echoes `splits` back with an `id` per entry, `[]` when there are none. Optional `tracking` object (`utmSource`, `utmMedium`, `utmCampaign`, `utmTerm`, `utmContent`, `src`, `sck`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `ttclid`, `gaClientId`, `fbp`, `fbc`) with attribution data for the conversion plugins: a malformed `gaClientId`, `fbp` or `fbc` is ignored, and an over-long value in another field returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; see the Payments guide. Optional `recoveryKit` boolean turns the buyer recovery e-mails on or off for a hosted payment (omitted: the account default); it is ignored in sandbox and does nothing on a headless payment. Optional `items` (1 to 50 lines; `amount` can be omitted and must match their sum when sent, `400 AMOUNT_ITEMS_MISMATCH`), `itemsQuantityEditable`, `couponCode` (`400 COUPON_INVALID` for any unusable code; a 100% discount returns `status: "FREE"` at once on a headless payment), and, hosted only (`OFFERS_REQUIRE_HOSTED` otherwise), `orderBump` and `upsell` (`400 UPSELL_AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH` above the payment amount after the coupon). The response carries `items`, `subtotal`, `discount` and `coupon`.
- [List payments](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/list): `GET /v1/payments` — each payment carries the same `payer`, `recoveryKit`, `items`, `subtotal`, `discount`, `coupon`, `parentPaymentId` and `completedAt` as the detail, except that `payer.email` and `payer.phone` do not fall back to the linked customer record. `status=FREE` lists free orders.
- [Get payment](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/get): `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` — paid PIX payments include a nullable `payer` block (name, document, institution name + ISPB) and `paidAt`. `payer` also carries `email` and `phone`: the ones the payer typed on the hosted checkout, else the ones sent in `customer` (or of the `customerId` customer) at creation, else, on this endpoint and on `/simulate` only, those of the customer record linked to the payment; `payer` is `null` only when all seven fields are unknown, so a `payer` with only contact data is possible before payment and is not a paid signal. Webhook `payer` blocks are unchanged. `recoveryKit` is `{ enabled, charged, emailsSent }`: whether the recovery kit is on for the payment, whether its price was debited, and how many recovery e-mails were sent. CARD payments carry masked card data in `methodData`, without `challengeUrl`, and `methodData.cardFundingType`: `credit`, `debit`, or `null` when the funding type is not known (older payments included). `methodData` is `null` while a boleto payment is `PROCESSING` after a `502`, and on a `FREE` payment. `items` (each with `kind` `ITEM`, `ORDER_BUMP` or `UPSELL`), `subtotal`, `discount` and `coupon` describe the order; `parentPaymentId` is set on a payment created by a post-purchase upsell; `completedAt` is set on a `FREE` payment, whose `paidAt` is `null`.
- [Get payment by txId](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/get-by-txid): `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}` — same `payer`, `recoveryKit` and order fields as the list.
- [Download boleto PDF](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/get-boleto): `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/boleto`
- [Refund payment](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/refund): `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refund` — a payment can be refunded once; a second refund returns `400 REFUND_ALREADY_PERFORMED` (after a partial refund) or `400 ALREADY_REFUNDED` (after a full one). A `FREE` payment returns `400 INVALID_STATUS`.
- [List refunds](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/payments/list-refunds): `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refunds` — `reason` is the one sent with the refund request, `Pedido de reembolso do comprador` for a payer's refund request approved by the merchant or automatically, `Reembolso feito pela YuvexPay` for the refund YuvexPay made after a payer's request (full amount debited, fee kept, balance can go negative), or `null` when none was sent and on refunds that reached YuvexPay from the payment network, such as the return of a PIX MED.
- [List split partners](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/splits/partners): `GET /v1/splits/partners` — the companies this account may split with, in both directions, for the environment of the API key. Fields: `id` (the relationship, not the company), `companyId` (send this as `recipientCompanyId`), `tradeName`, `direction` (`OUTGOING`/`INCOMING`), `status`, `feeCap` (the fee cap recorded on a relationship with an approved split platform, in percent of `amount`, as a string with two decimal places, or `null` for an ordinary partner), `requestedAt`, `acceptedAt`. Optional `status` and `direction` filters. Every partner is returned in one response, newest first, unless `limit` (1 to 100) is sent: then at most `limit` relationships are read per call, the response carries `nextCursor`, to send back as `cursor` until it is `null`, and a page can carry fewer partners than `limit`. `nextCursor` is `null` when the whole list was returned. **Only `ACCEPTED` is usable in `splits[]`.** Requires the `payments:read` scope. There is no API to invite, accept, decline or revoke — that is dashboard-only; the one exception is an approved split platform connecting a seller through `X-Split-Platform-Key` on `POST /v1/payments`.
- [Balance](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/balance/get): `GET /v1/balance` — a split credit received from another YuvexPay company follows **your own** rolling reserve policy, not the originating company's. Together with `GET /v1/documents/statements` this is the only public record a split recipient has of the money — the payment itself belongs to the originating company.
- [Create withdrawal](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/create): `POST /v1/withdrawals` — optional `destination.recipientDocument` (CPF/CNPJ of the PIX key holder); send it for any third-party payout.
- [List withdrawals](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/list): `GET /v1/withdrawals` — no `errorMessage` and no `isSandbox`; `providerErrorCode` is present.
- [Get withdrawal](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/get): `GET /v1/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}` — carries `errorMessage` and `providerErrorCode`.
- [Withdrawal limits](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/withdrawals/limits): `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits` — daily/nightly window, `minAmount` and `perTransactionLimit`.
- [Create product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/create): `POST /v1/products`
- [List products](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/list): `GET /v1/products`
- [Get product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/get): `GET /v1/products/{productId}`
- [Get product by external id](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/get-by-external-id): `GET /v1/products/external/{externalId}`
- [Update product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/update): `PATCH /v1/products/{productId}`
- [Delete product](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/delete): `DELETE /v1/products/{productId}`
- [Upload product image](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/upload-image): `POST /v1/products/{productId}/image`
- [Delete product image](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/products/delete-image): `DELETE /v1/products/{productId}/image`
- [Create coupon](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/coupons/create): `POST /v1/coupons` — `coupons:write`; `X-Idempotency-Key` optional. `code` (3 to 32 of `A-Z`, `0-9`, `_`, `-`, stored uppercase, unique per account and environment among coupons not deleted, else `409 COUPON_CODE_TAKEN`), `type` `PERCENT` with `percentBp` (1-10000) or `FIXED` with `amount` (`400 COUPON_VALUE_INVALID` otherwise), optional `validFrom`/`validUntil` (`400 COUPON_WINDOW_INVALID` when not in order), `maxRedemptions`, `maxRedemptionsPerBuyer`, `productIds` (up to 100, `400 COUPON_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`), `active` (default `true`). Returns `{ coupon }` with `redemptionCount`, the uses held by open payments plus completed ones.
- [List coupons](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/coupons/list): `GET /v1/coupons` — `coupons:read`; coupons not deleted in the key's environment, newest first; `search` (code contains, case-insensitive), `active` (`true`/`false`), `page`, `limit`.
- [Get coupon](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/coupons/get): `GET /v1/coupons/{couponId}` — `coupons:read`; a deleted coupon or one from the other environment returns `404`.
- [Update coupon](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/coupons/update): `PATCH /v1/coupons/{couponId}` — `coupons:write`; send only the fields to change, `null` clears a nullable one, changing `type` needs the new type's value; payments already holding the coupon keep it.
- [Delete coupon](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/coupons/delete): `DELETE /v1/coupons/{couponId}` — `coupons:write`; soft delete: the coupon is deactivated, leaves the list, `GET` returns `404` and its code can be reused; payments already holding it keep their discount. Returns `{ message }`.
- [Create customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/create): `POST /v1/customers`
- [List customers](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/list): `GET /v1/customers`
- [Get customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/get): `GET /v1/customers/{customerId}` — `customerId` is a `cus_*` slug, not a UUID.
- [Update customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/update): `PATCH /v1/customers/{customerId}`
- [Delete customer](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/customers/delete): `DELETE /v1/customers/{customerId}`
- [Payment receipt](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/documents/payment-receipt): `GET /v1/documents/payments/{paymentId}/receipt` — scoped to the key's environment; an id from the other environment returns `404`. Only `PAID` and `REFUNDED` payments have a receipt; a `FREE` one returns `400 RECEIPT_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
- [Withdrawal receipt](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/documents/withdrawal-receipt): `GET /v1/documents/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}/receipt` — same environment scoping.
- [Account statement](https://docs.yuvexpay.com/api-reference/documents/statement): `GET /v1/documents/statements` — built from the real-money ledger, so a sandbox key always gets an empty statement. A recovery kit price appears as a debit labelled `Kit de recuperação`, and the fee of a free order as a debit labelled `Taxa de pedido gratuito`.
